#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Integration: run-level wall-clock limit with watchdog (#1944)
#
# SPEC-1 [code]: a run whose wall-clock time exceeds max_run_s ends with
#   pipeline status timed_out in pipeline-state.json and pipeline.end event
#   carrying status=timed_out, the in-flight stage, and limit_s; the watchdog
#   fires even when the engine is idle between dispatches (not only inside a
#   stage); a process that ignores TERM is dead within TERM + 10 s; release and
#   persist execute on every timed-out exit path.
#
# Phases:
#   P1 — basic timeout: slow stage hits the watchdog; status=timed_out, event
#        fields correct; runner exits non-zero within the limit
#   P2 — idle between dispatches: fast-one completes before watchdog fires;
#        watchdog fires while fast-two is sleeping; fast-one being in "complete"
#        state proves the watchdog runs independently of stage dispatch state
#   P3 — TERM-ignore: a stage that traps and ignores SIGTERM is dead within
#        TERM + 10 s (KILL escalation)
#   P4 — release and persist run: always_run release + persist stages execute
#        on every timed-out exit path
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "run-timed-out: wall-clock limit watchdog fires and ends run correctly (#1944)"
setup_test_env "run-timed-out"
export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn

PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"
STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state"
EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events"
EVENTS_JSONL="$EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$PLUGINS_ROOT"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$EVENTS_DIR"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$EVENTS_JSONL"
export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
export ZBUILD_MODELS_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/config/models.json"
export ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0
export ZBUILD_SCOPE_OVERRIDE=1
mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR" "$EVENTS_DIR" "$HOME/.zbuild"
printf '%s' "bootstrap" > "$HOME/.zbuild/scope-override-token"

# ── Shared overlay repo ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
OVERLAY_REPO="$(setup_git_temp_repo run-timed-out-overlay)"
mkdir -p "$OVERLAY_REPO/.zbuild/templates"

# Single-stage template: one slow stage (the main timeout victim)
cat > "$OVERLAY_REPO/.zbuild/templates/timeout-single.yaml" <<'EOF'
id: timeout-single
extends: simple
stages:
  - id: slow-stage
    gate: auto
    io:
      destinations: [file]
      tail_lines: 50
    router:
      timeout_s: 120
      max_turns: 0
EOF

# Two-stage template: fast-one is instant; fast-two blocks for a long time
cat > "$OVERLAY_REPO/.zbuild/templates/timeout-two-stage.yaml" <<'EOF'
id: timeout-two-stage
extends: simple
stages:
  - id: fast-one
    gate: auto
    io:
      destinations: [file]
      tail_lines: 50
  - id: fast-two
    gate: auto
    io:
      destinations: [file]
      tail_lines: 50
EOF

# Always-run (release + persist) template: flow stage + always_run release + persist
cat > "$OVERLAY_REPO/.zbuild/templates/timeout-with-release.yaml" <<'EOF'
id: timeout-with-release
extends: simple
flow:
  - outcome

always_run:
  - release
  - persist-stage

outcome:
  gate: auto
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50

release:
  gate: auto
  roles: [teardown]
  router:
    timeout_s: 30
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50

persist-stage:
  gate: auto
  roles: [persist]
  router:
    timeout_s: 30
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50
EOF

# Commit the templates into the overlay repo so the runner can find them
(cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && git add .zbuild && git commit -q -m "add timeout test templates") >/dev/null 2>&1

# ── P1: basic timeout — slow stage, status=timed_out ───────────────────────

# Stage that sleeps far longer than max_run_s
mock_plugin_factory "slow-stage" "agent" 0 >/dev/null
SLOW_STAGE_STARTED="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/slow-stage-started"
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/slow-stage/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
slow_stage_run() {
    : > "${SLOW_STAGE_STARTED}"
    sleep 120
    $(mock_result_line slow-stage)
    return 0
}
PLUG

export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$STATE_DIR"
print_test_section "P1: slow stage timeout — status=timed_out written to pipeline-state.json"

# Run with ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=2 (2 seconds); wrap in timeout 25s to prevent hanging
# before implementation (no watchdog → stage sleeps forever → outer timeout kills it)
p1_rc=0
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=2 timeout 25 bash "$RUNNER" \
    --template timeout-single --goal "run-timed-out test p1" ) \
    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p1.stdout" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p1.stderr" \
    || p1_rc=$?

STATE_FILE="$STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json"

# Runner must exit non-zero (timed-out runs are failures)
assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: runner exits non-zero" "1" "$p1_rc"

# pipeline-state.json must exist and have status=timed_out
if [[ ! -f "$STATE_FILE" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: pipeline-state.json written" "state file not found"
else
    _p1_status="$(jq -r '.status // empty' "$STATE_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: pipeline-state.json status=timed_out" "timed_out" "$_p1_status"
fi

print_test_section "P1: pipeline.end event fields — status=timed_out, stage, limit_s"

if [[ ! -f "$EVENTS_JSONL" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: events.jsonl written" "events file not found"
else
    # Event: pipeline.end with status=timed_out
    _p1_end_event="$(jq -c 'select(.type=="pipeline.end" and .data.status=="timed_out")' \
        "$EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | tail -1)"
    if [[ -n "$_p1_end_event" ]]; then
        assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: pipeline.end status=timed_out event emitted"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: pipeline.end status=timed_out event emitted" \
            "no such event in $(wc -l < "$EVENTS_JSONL") events"
    fi

    # The event must carry the in-flight stage name
    _p1_stage="$(jq -r 'select(.type=="pipeline.end" and .data.status=="timed_out") | .data.stage // empty' \
        "$EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | tail -1)"
    if [[ -n "$_p1_stage" ]]; then
        assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: pipeline.end event carries in-flight stage (stage=$_p1_stage)"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: pipeline.end event carries in-flight stage" \
            "stage field empty in timed_out pipeline.end event"
    fi

    # The event must carry limit_s (the max_run_s value that was applied)
    _p1_limit="$(jq -r 'select(.type=="pipeline.end" and .data.status=="timed_out") | .data.limit_s // empty' \
        "$EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | tail -1)"
    if [[ -n "$_p1_limit" && "$_p1_limit" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
        assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: pipeline.end event carries limit_s=$_p1_limit"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: pipeline.end event carries limit_s" \
            "limit_s field absent or non-numeric in timed_out pipeline.end event"
    fi
fi

# ── P2: idle between dispatches — watchdog fires independently of stage state ─
print_test_section "P2: watchdog fires even when engine is idle between dispatches"

# Reset state/events for fresh run
rm -f "$STATE_FILE" "$EVENTS_JSONL"
mock_plugin_factory "fast-one" "agent" 0 >/dev/null
mock_plugin_factory "fast-two" "agent" 0 >/dev/null

# fast-one: returns immediately (proves it can complete BEFORE the watchdog fires)
# fast-two: sleeps 30s (watchdog fires during fast-two's execution)
# max_run_s=3: watchdog fires 3s into the run. fast-one completes in < 1s.
# After 3s, fast-one's status in pipeline-state.json MUST be "complete", proving
# the watchdog ran independently — it did not need a stage to be dispatching.
# If the watchdog fired BEFORE fast-one completed, fast-one's status would not be
# "complete", and the assertion below would fail.
FAST_TWO_STARTED="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/fast-two-started"
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/fast-one/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
fast_one_run() {
    $(mock_result_line fast-one)
    return 0
}
PLUG
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/fast-two/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
fast_two_run() {
    : > "${FAST_TWO_STARTED}"
    sleep 30
    $(mock_result_line fast-two)
    return 0
}
PLUG

p2_rc=0
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=3 timeout 25 bash "$RUNNER" \
    --template timeout-two-stage --goal "run-timed-out test p2" ) \
    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p2.stdout" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p2.stderr" \
    || p2_rc=$?

assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-1] P2: runner exits non-zero" "1" "$p2_rc"

if [[ -f "$STATE_FILE" ]]; then
    _p2_status="$(jq -r '.status // empty' "$STATE_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-1] P2: pipeline status=timed_out (watchdog fires regardless of dispatch state)" \
        "timed_out" "$_p2_status"

    # fast-one MUST have completed before the watchdog fired: its status must be
    # "complete". This is the falsifiable check — if the watchdog fired before
    # fast-one completed, fast-one's status would not be "complete" and this fails.
    # Stage names are stored with their literal name (hyphenated) as the key.
    _p2_fast_one="$(jq -r '.stage_statuses["fast-one"] // empty' "$STATE_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [[ "$_p2_fast_one" == "complete" ]]; then
        assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-1] P2: fast-one completed before watchdog fired (watchdog fires independently)"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P2: fast-one completed before watchdog fired" \
            "fast-one status: '${_p2_fast_one:-<empty>}' — watchdog fired too early or fast-one did not run"
    fi
else
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P2: pipeline-state.json written" "state file not found"
fi

# ── P3: TERM-ignore → KILL within TERM + 10s ────────────────────────────────
print_test_section "P3: stage that ignores SIGTERM is dead within TERM + 10s"

rm -f "$STATE_FILE" "$EVENTS_JSONL"

# Stage that traps SIGTERM and does NOT exit, sleeps indefinitely
TERM_IGNORED_PID_FILE="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/term-ignore-pid"
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/slow-stage/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
slow_stage_run() {
    : > "${SLOW_STAGE_STARTED}"
    # Record our PID so the test can check it is dead
    printf '%s\n' "\$\$" > "${TERM_IGNORED_PID_FILE}"
    # Trap SIGTERM and ignore it (only SIGKILL can stop this)
    trap '' TERM
    sleep 120
    $(mock_result_line slow-stage)
    return 0
}
PLUG

_p3_start="$(date +%s)"
# max_run_s=2 → watchdog fires at 2s, sends TERM; stage ignores it;
# watchdog escalates to KILL at 2+10=12s. The runner must exit within ~15s.
p3_rc=0
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=2 timeout 30 bash "$RUNNER" \
    --template timeout-single --goal "run-timed-out test p3 term-ignore" ) \
    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p3.stdout" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p3.stderr" \
    || p3_rc=$?
_p3_elapsed=$(( $(date +%s) - _p3_start ))

# Runner must exit (not hang past 30s timeout)
assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-1] P3: runner exits non-zero (not still running)" "1" "$p3_rc"

# Runner must exit within TERM + 10s + buffer = 2 + 10 + 5 = 17s
if [[ "$_p3_elapsed" -le 17 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-1] P3: runner exits within TERM+10s+buffer (elapsed ${_p3_elapsed}s)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P3: runner exits within TERM+10s+buffer" \
        "elapsed ${_p3_elapsed}s > 17s"
fi

# If stage PID was written, check the process is dead
if [[ -f "$TERM_IGNORED_PID_FILE" ]]; then
    _ignore_pid="$(cat "$TERM_IGNORED_PID_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [[ "$_ignore_pid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
        if kill -0 "$_ignore_pid" 2>/dev/null; then
            assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P3: TERM-ignoring stage process is dead after TERM+10s" \
                "PID $_ignore_pid is still alive"
        else
            assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-1] P3: TERM-ignoring stage process is dead (PID $_ignore_pid killed)"
        fi
    fi
fi

# ── P4: release AND persist stages run on timed-out exit path ───────────────
print_test_section "P4: always_run release and persist stages execute on timed-out exit path"

rm -f "$STATE_FILE" "$EVENTS_JSONL"

mock_plugin_factory "outcome"       "agent" 0 "" ""        >/dev/null
mock_plugin_factory "teardown"      "tool"  0 "" "teardown" >/dev/null
mock_plugin_factory "persist-stage" "tool"  0 "" "persist"  >/dev/null

# Outcome (flow) stage: sleeps 30s (will be killed by watchdog)
OUTCOME_STARTED="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/outcome-started"
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/outcome/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
outcome_run() {
    : > "${OUTCOME_STARTED}"
    sleep 30
    $(mock_result_line outcome)
    return 0
}
PLUG

# Release (teardown) stage: drops a marker to prove it ran
RELEASE_MARKER="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/release-ran-on-timeout"
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/teardown/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
teardown_run() {
    : > "${RELEASE_MARKER}"
    $(mock_result_line teardown)
    return 0
}
PLUG

# Persist stage: drops a marker to prove it ran
PERSIST_MARKER="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/persist-ran-on-timeout"
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/persist-stage/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
persist_stage_run() {
    : > "${PERSIST_MARKER}"
    $(mock_result_line persist-stage)
    return 0
}
PLUG

p4_rc=0
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=2 timeout 25 bash "$RUNNER" \
    --template timeout-with-release --goal "run-timed-out test p4 release+persist" ) \
    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p4.stdout" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p4.stderr" \
    || p4_rc=$?

assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-1] P4: runner exits non-zero on timed-out path" "1" "$p4_rc"

if [[ -f "$STATE_FILE" ]]; then
    _p4_status="$(jq -r '.status // empty' "$STATE_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-1] P4: pipeline status=timed_out" "timed_out" "$_p4_status"
else
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P4: pipeline-state.json written" "state file not found"
fi

if [[ -e "$RELEASE_MARKER" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-1] P4: release (always_run) stage ran on timed-out exit path"
else
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P4: release (always_run) stage ran on timed-out exit path" \
        "release marker not found — always_run release stage did not execute"
fi

if [[ -e "$PERSIST_MARKER" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-1] P4: persist (always_run) stage ran on timed-out exit path"
else
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P4: persist (always_run) stage ran on timed-out exit path" \
        "persist marker not found — always_run persist stage did not execute"
fi

print_test_results
exit $((FAIL > 0))

250	# abort with rc=1 before any stage dispatches. This exercises template.sh's
251	# template_max_run_s() function, which is called by _runner_resolve_run_limit_s.

418	# run-open-items.sh adds timed_out to run_end_words. If reverted, the

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tests/unit/run-limit-precedence-test.sh — run-level wall-clock limit (#1944)
#
# SPEC-2 [code]:
#   _runner_resolve_run_limit_s resolves template max_run_s > ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S >
#   20700; a non-integer or non-positive value in template or env yields
#   disposition misconfigured and the run does not reach the dispatch loop.
#
# SPEC-5 [no-code]:
#   The limit is resolved from template, env, or constant only; scripts/lib/
#   stage-limits.sh and core/pipeline/runner.sh contain no reference to
#   GITHUB_ACTIONS, CI, or any platform-specific variable in the new code.
#
# SPEC-6 [no-code]:
#   ADR-025 names timed_out in its word vocabulary with ## Enforced by entries
#   citing the new tests; ADR-054 gains a §11 for the run-level limit with
#   ## Enforced by; config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt no longer lists
#   ADR-054-stage-contract.md.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "run-limit-precedence: max_run_s resolution + platform-free + ADR alignment (#1944)"
setup_test_env "run-limit-precedence"

RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"
STAGE_LIMITS="$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/stage-limits.sh"

# ─── SPEC-2: _runner_resolve_run_limit_s ────────────────────────────────────

print_test_section "[#1944/SPEC-2] _runner_resolve_run_limit_s is defined in stage-limits.sh"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/stage-limits.sh
source "$STAGE_LIMITS" 2>/dev/null || true

if declare -F _runner_resolve_run_limit_s >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-2] _runner_resolve_run_limit_s is defined in stage-limits.sh"
else
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-2] _runner_resolve_run_limit_s is defined in stage-limits.sh" \
        "function not found after sourcing scripts/lib/stage-limits.sh"
fi

print_test_section "[#1944/SPEC-2] precedence: template max_run_s > ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S > 20700"

if declare -F _runner_resolve_run_limit_s >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    # Case 1: no template value, no env → falls back to default 20700
    _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""
    template_max_run_s() { printf ''; }
    unset ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S
    _runner_resolve_run_limit_s 2>/dev/null || true
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] no template, no env → default 20700" "20700" "${_RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S:-}"

    # Case 2: env only → uses env
    _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""
    template_max_run_s() { printf ''; }
    ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=3600
    _runner_resolve_run_limit_s 2>/dev/null || true
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] env ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=3600 used when no template value" "3600" "${_RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S:-}"
    unset ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S

    # Case 3: template value > env → template wins
    _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""
    template_max_run_s() { printf '7200'; }
    ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=3600
    _runner_resolve_run_limit_s 2>/dev/null || true
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] template value wins over ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S" "7200" "${_RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S:-}"
    unset ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S

    # Case 4: template value only (no env) → template wins over default
    _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""
    template_max_run_s() { printf '1800'; }
    unset ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S
    _runner_resolve_run_limit_s 2>/dev/null || true
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] template value wins over default" "1800" "${_RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S:-}"
else
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-2] precedence checks skipped — function not found" "missing implementation"
fi

print_test_section "[#1944/SPEC-2] non-integer / non-positive → misconfigured, rc=1"

if declare -F _runner_resolve_run_limit_s >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    # Non-integer in template
    _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""
    template_max_run_s() { printf 'not-a-number'; }
    unset ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S
    _rc2=0
    _runner_resolve_run_limit_s 2>/dev/null || _rc2=$?
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] non-integer template value → rc=1" "1" "$_rc2"

    # Non-positive (zero) in template
    _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""
    template_max_run_s() { printf '0'; }
    unset ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S
    _rc2=0
    _runner_resolve_run_limit_s 2>/dev/null || _rc2=$?
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] template value=0 → rc=1" "1" "$_rc2"

    # Negative in template
    _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""
    template_max_run_s() { printf -- '-5'; }
    unset ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S
    _rc2=0
    _runner_resolve_run_limit_s 2>/dev/null || _rc2=$?
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] negative template value → rc=1" "1" "$_rc2"

    # Non-integer in ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S
    _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""
    template_max_run_s() { printf ''; }
    ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S="thirty"
    _rc2=0
    _runner_resolve_run_limit_s 2>/dev/null || _rc2=$?
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] non-integer ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S → rc=1" "1" "$_rc2"
    unset ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S

    # Non-positive in ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S
    _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""
    template_max_run_s() { printf ''; }
    ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=0
    _rc2=0
    _runner_resolve_run_limit_s 2>/dev/null || _rc2=$?
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=0 → rc=1" "1" "$_rc2"
    unset ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S
else
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-2] validation checks skipped — function not found" "missing implementation"
fi

# ─── SPEC-2: template_max_run_s() from the real template.sh ─────────────────
# This section sources the REAL template.sh to test its template_max_run_s()
# function directly. If template.sh is reverted (function removed), the
# assert_fail below fires — making template.sh testable.
print_test_section "[#1944/SPEC-2] template_max_run_s() reads max_run_s from template YAML (real function)"
TEMPLATE_SH="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/template.sh"

# shellcheck source=../../core/pipeline/template.sh
source "$TEMPLATE_SH" 2>/dev/null || true

# Build two YAML fixtures: one WITH max_run_s, one WITHOUT
_tpl_yaml="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/max-run-test.yaml"
cat > "$_tpl_yaml" <<'EOF'
id: max-run-test
max_run_s: 3600
extends: simple
EOF

_tpl_none="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/no-max-run.yaml"
cat > "$_tpl_none" <<'EOF'
id: no-max-run-test
extends: simple
EOF

if declare -F template_max_run_s >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    # Real function from template.sh: must extract the value from the YAML.
    _TPL_SOURCE_FILE="$_tpl_yaml"
    _tmr="$(template_max_run_s 2>/dev/null || true)"
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] template_max_run_s() returns max_run_s value from YAML" "3600" "$_tmr"

    # When max_run_s is absent, function returns empty (no override)
    _TPL_SOURCE_FILE="$_tpl_none"
    _tmr_empty="$(template_max_run_s 2>/dev/null || true)"
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] template_max_run_s() returns empty when max_run_s absent" "" "$_tmr_empty"
    unset _TPL_SOURCE_FILE
else
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-2] template_max_run_s() defined in core/pipeline/template.sh" \
        "function not found after sourcing template.sh — implementation missing or template.sh reverted"
fi

print_test_section "[#1944/SPEC-2] misconfigured run (invalid ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S): runner rejects before dispatch"
# Run the actual runner with an invalid ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S; it must exit non-zero
# before dispatching any stage (no stage marker written).
export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"
export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-miscfg"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events-miscfg"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn
export ZBUILD_MODELS_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/config/models.json"
export ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0
export ZBUILD_SCOPE_OVERRIDE=1
mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR" "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR" "$HOME/.zbuild"
printf '%s' "bootstrap" > "$HOME/.zbuild/scope-override-token"

# Minimal single-stage plugin
mock_plugin_factory "intake" "agent" 0 >/dev/null

MISCFG_OVERLAY="$(setup_git_temp_repo miscfg-run-limit)"
mkdir -p "$MISCFG_OVERLAY/.zbuild/templates"
cat > "$MISCFG_OVERLAY/.zbuild/templates/limit-single.yaml" <<'EOF'
id: limit-single
extends: simple
stages:
  - id: intake
    gate: auto
    io:
      destinations: [file]
      tail_lines: 50
EOF

STAGE_MARKER="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/stage-ran-marker"
cat > "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins/agent/intake/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
intake_run() {
    : > "${STAGE_MARKER}"
    $(mock_result_line intake)
    return 0
}
PLUG

# Run with invalid env var — must fail before dispatch loop
_miscfg_rc=0
( cd "$MISCFG_OVERLAY" && ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S="not-a-number" bash "$RUNNER" \
    --template limit-single --goal "test misconfigured limit" ) \
    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/miscfg.stdout" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/miscfg.stderr" \
    || _miscfg_rc=$?

assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] invalid ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S → runner exits non-zero" "1" "$_miscfg_rc"
if [[ -e "$STAGE_MARKER" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-2] stage did not run when env limit is misconfigured" \
        "stage marker exists — dispatch loop was reached"
else
    assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-2] stage did not run when env limit is misconfigured"
fi

# Check that misconfigured is explained AND names the source (ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S)
_miscfg_sf="$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json"
if [[ -f "$_miscfg_sf" ]]; then
    _miscfg_disp="$(jq -r '.disposition // empty' "$_miscfg_sf" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] pipeline-state.json disposition=misconfigured (env)" "misconfigured" "$_miscfg_disp"
fi
# Collect output: prefer state file reason field, fall back to stderr+stdout
_miscfg_all_output=""
if [[ -f "$_miscfg_sf" ]]; then

# ── P2: idle between dispatches — watchdog fires independently of stage state ─
print_test_section "P2: watchdog fires even when engine is idle between dispatches"

# Reset state/events for fresh run
rm -f "$STATE_FILE" "$EVENTS_JSONL"
mock_plugin_factory "fast-one" "agent" 0 >/dev/null
mock_plugin_factory "fast-two" "agent" 0 >/dev/null

# fast-one: returns immediately (proves it can complete BEFORE the watchdog fires)
# fast-two: sleeps 30s (watchdog fires during fast-two's execution)
# max_run_s=3: watchdog fires 3s into the run. fast-one completes in < 1s.
# After 3s, fast-one's status in pipeline-state.json MUST be "complete", proving
# the watchdog ran independently — it did not need a stage to be dispatching.
# If the watchdog fired BEFORE fast-one completed, fast-one's status would not be
# "complete", and the assertion below would fail.
FAST_TWO_STARTED="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/fast-two-started"
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/fast-one/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
fast_one_run() {
    $(mock_result_line fast-one)
    return 0
}
PLUG
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/fast-two/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
fast_two_run() {
    : > "${FAST_TWO_STARTED}"
    sleep 30
    $(mock_result_line fast-two)
    return 0
}
PLUG

p2_rc=0
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=3 timeout 25 bash "$RUNNER" \
    --template timeout-two-stage --goal "run-timed-out test p2" ) \
    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p2.stdout" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p2.stderr" \
    || p2_rc=$?

assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-1] P2: runner exits non-zero" "1" "$p2_rc"

if [[ -f "$STATE_FILE" ]]; then
    _p2_status="$(jq -r '.status // empty' "$STATE_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-1] P2: pipeline status=timed_out (watchdog fires regardless of dispatch state)" \
        "timed_out" "$_p2_status"

    # fast-one MUST have completed before the watchdog fired: its status must be
    # "complete". This is the falsifiable check — if the watchdog fired before
    # fast-one completed, fast-one's status would not be "complete" and this fails.
    # Stage names are stored with their literal name (hyphenated) as the key.
    _p2_fast_one="$(jq -r '.stage_statuses["fast-one"] // empty' "$STATE_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [[ "$_p2_fast_one" == "complete" ]]; then
        assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-1] P2: fast-one completed before watchdog fired (watchdog fires independently)"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P2: fast-one completed before watchdog fired" \
            "fast-one status: '${_p2_fast_one:-<empty>}' — watchdog fired too early or fast-one did not run"
    fi
else
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P2: pipeline-state.json written" "state file not found"
fi

# ── P3: TERM-ignore → KILL within TERM + 10s ────────────────────────────────
print_test_section "P3: stage that ignores SIGTERM is dead within TERM + 10s"

rm -f "$STATE_FILE" "$EVENTS_JSONL"

# Stage that traps SIGTERM and does NOT exit, sleeps indefinitely
TERM_IGNORED_PID_FILE="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/term-ignore-pid"
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/slow-stage/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
slow_stage_run() {
    : > "${SLOW_STAGE_STARTED}"
    # Record our PID so the test can check it is dead
    printf '%s\n' "\$\$" > "${TERM_IGNORED_PID_FILE}"
    # Trap SIGTERM and ignore it (only SIGKILL can stop this)
    trap '' TERM
    sleep 120
    $(mock_result_line slow-stage)
    return 0
}
PLUG

_p3_start="$(date +%s)"
# max_run_s=2 → watchdog fires at 2s, sends TERM; stage ignores it;
# watchdog escalates to KILL at 2+10=12s. The runner must exit within ~15s.
p3_rc=0
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=2 timeout 30 bash "$RUNNER" \
    --template timeout-single --goal "run-timed-out test p3 term-ignore" ) \
    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p3.stdout" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p3.stderr" \
    || p3_rc=$?
_p3_elapsed=$(( $(date +%s) - _p3_start ))

# Runner must exit (not hang past 30s timeout)
assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-1] P3: runner exits non-zero (not still running)" "1" "$p3_rc"

# Runner must exit within TERM + 10s + buffer = 2 + 10 + 5 = 17s
if [[ "$_p3_elapsed" -le 17 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-1] P3: runner exits within TERM+10s+buffer (elapsed ${_p3_elapsed}s)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P3: runner exits within TERM+10s+buffer" \
        "elapsed ${_p3_elapsed}s > 17s"
fi

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
3	# ║  zBuild test-helpers — Shared test harness for all unit tests        ║
4	# ║  Source this from any *-test.sh file to get assert_*, setup, teardown    ║
5	# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
6	#
7	# Usage:
8	#   SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)"
9	#   source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/test-helpers.sh"
10	#
11	# Provides:
12	#   Colors, counters, assert_pass/fail/eq/contains/contains_regex/gt/json_key
13	#   setup_test_env / cleanup_test_env  (temp dir, mock PATH, mock HOME)
14	#   print_test_header / print_test_results
15	#   Mock helpers: mock_binary, mock_jq, mock_git, mock_gh, mock_claude
16	
17	[[ -n "${_TEST_HELPERS_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
18	_TEST_HELPERS_LOADED=1
19	
20	# ─── Re-entrancy guard (#971): refuse a test invoked inside another test run ──
21	# Every *-test.sh sources this file first, so this is the universal chokepoint.
22	# A test executed from WITHIN another test run — e.g. the ablation negctl/
23	# reachability gates run `bash <changed-test>` directly — would re-enter the gate
24	# logic and fork-bomb the pipeline test stage (the recurring #929/#983/#971 class).
25	# The #983 guard in run-tests.sh only catches run-tests.sh-mediated nesting; the
26	# ablation's direct `bash` bypasses it. This guard catches BOTH paths.
27	# The sentinel has NO leading underscore so env-scrub's ^(ZBUILD_|_TPL_) clears it
28	# at every fresh-user-shell boundary (the pipeline test stage), avoiding a stale-
29	# value false refusal. Fixture-isolated nested runs set ZBUILD_TESTS_DIR and are
30	# exempt (mirrors the #983 guard's exemption). The guard fires ONLY when $0 is a
31	# `*-test.sh` being EXECUTED (`bash <test>.sh` — the ablation/fork-bomb path), not
32	# when a script merely sources this file for introspection (`bash -c "source …"`,
33	# where $0 is `bash`) — so test-helpers' own self-tests are unaffected.
34	if [[ -n "${ZBUILD_TEST_EXEC_ACTIVE:-}" && -z "${ZBUILD_TESTS_DIR:-}" && "${0##*/}" == *-test.sh ]]; then
35	    echo "test-helpers.sh: refusing nested test invocation (re-entrancy guard #971)" >&2
36	    exit 2
37	fi
38	export ZBUILD_TEST_EXEC_ACTIVE=1
39	
40	# The vision admission gate (ADR-049 / #1360) enforces a conforming vision doc by
41	# default. Fixture-based tests spin up temp repos with no vision doc and are not
42	# testing vision, so they must opt out — same hermeticity precedent as
43	# ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR. Tests that DO exercise the gate set the mode inline
44	# per-case, which overrides this default. Real (non-test) runs never source this
45	# file, so dogfood-on-zbuild still enforces against the real .zbuild/vision.md.
46	export ZBUILD_VISION_GATE="${ZBUILD_VISION_GATE:-off}"
47	
48	# ─── Colors ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
49	CYAN='\033[38;2;0;212;255m'
50	GREEN='\033[38;2;74;222;128m'
51	RED='\033[38;2;248;113;113m'
52	# shellcheck disable=SC2034
53	YELLOW='\033[38;2;250;204;21m'
54	# shellcheck disable=SC2034
55	PURPLE='\033[38;2;168;85;247m'
56	DIM='\033[2m'
57	BOLD='\033[1m'
58	RESET='\033[0m'
59	
60	# ─── Counters ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
61	PASS=0
62	FAIL=0
63	TOTAL=0
64	SKIP=0
65	FAILURES=()
66	
67	# ─── Auto-initialize TEST_TEMP_DIR ──────────────────────────────────────────
68	# Many test files use TEST_TEMP_DIR in their setup_env() without calling
69	# setup_test_env(). Auto-create a temp dir so $TEST_TEMP_DIR is never empty.
70	# Save originals now so cleanup_test_env() can always restore them.
71	ORIG_HOME="${HOME}"
72	ORIG_PATH="${PATH}"
73	# Sandbox ZBUILD_STATE_DIR and ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR so stage-io writes during
74	# tests never escape to the outer pipeline's state directory (#1713).
75	# `+set` records SET-ness separately from the value: `${VAR:-}` collapses "unset"
76	# and "set but empty" into the same "", and cleanup would then unset a variable
77	# the caller had deliberately exported as empty. `${VAR-}` (no colon) keeps an
78	# empty value as empty.
79	ORIG_STATE_DIR_SET="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR+set}"
80	ORIG_STATE_DIR="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR-}"
81	ORIG_ARTIFACT_DIR_SET="${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR+set}"
82	ORIG_ARTIFACT_DIR="${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR-}"
83	# Track the auto-created temp dir separately so cleanup always removes it,
84	# even if individual tests later reassign TEST_TEMP_DIR in their own setup_env.
85	AUTO_TEST_TEMP_DIR=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/zb-test-auto.XXXXXX")
86	TEST_TEMP_DIR="$AUTO_TEST_TEMP_DIR"
87	# Wave 19-L (#751 Copilot review): freeze the tmp-root at source time so
88	# the master trap's prefix guard stays valid even when tests re-export
89	# TMPDIR (e.g., to $TEST_TEMP_DIR/_tmp for sandbox mktemp shims).
90	_ZB_TEST_TMP_ROOT="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}"
91	_ZB_TEST_TMP_ROOT="${_ZB_TEST_TMP_ROOT%/}"
92	mkdir -p "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/home/.zbuild"
93	mkdir -p "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin"
94	mkdir -p "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/_tmp"
95	# Sandbox mktemp shim — macOS plain `mktemp`/`mktemp -d` (no template) ignores
96	# $TMPDIR and uses /var/folders which is write-blocked in the sandbox.
97	# Route templateless calls through a writable directory.
98	# Linux mktemp respects $TMPDIR natively so no shim is needed there; installing
99	# one would break test setup_env() loops that do `ln -sf "$(command -v mktemp)"`
100	# because command -v resolves to the shim itself (same-file ln error).
101	if [[ "$(uname -s 2>/dev/null)" == "Darwin" ]]; then
102	    printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\n_s="%s"\nif [[ $# -eq 0 ]]; then exec /usr/bin/mktemp "$_s/tmp.XXXXXX"; fi\nif [[ $# -eq 1 && "$1" == "-d" ]]; then exec /usr/bin/mktemp -d "$_s/tmpd.XXXXXX"; fi\nexec /usr/bin/mktemp "$@"\n' \
103	        "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/_tmp" > "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/mktemp"
104	    chmod +x "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/mktemp"
105	fi
106	export PATH="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin:$PATH"
107	# ─── Child-process killer (used by master trap) ──────────────────────────────
108	_kill_test_children() {
109	    local pids
110	    pids=$(jobs -p 2>/dev/null) || true
111	    # shellcheck disable=SC2086  # word splitting intentional to pass multiple PIDs
112	    [[ -n "$pids" ]] && kill $pids 2>/dev/null || true
113	    pkill -P $$ 2>/dev/null || true
114	    wait 2>/dev/null || true
115	}
116	
117	# ─── Script-level cleanup hook — override in each test script ────────────────
118	# Default is a no-op; scripts set: _test_cleanup_hook() { cleanup_env; }
119	_test_cleanup_hook() { :; }
120	
121	# ─── Master trap — kills children, calls hook, removes auto temp dir ─────────
122	# _HARNESS_SIGNAL: set by dedicated INT/TERM wrappers before calling cleanup,
123	# so _test_harness_cleanup can re-raise and exit 128+signal instead of
124	# returning into the interrupted test body (which would produce bogus failures).
125	# _HARNESS_CLEANED_UP: idempotency guard — prevents double cleanup when both
126	# a signal handler and the EXIT trap would otherwise call the body.
127	_HARNESS_SIGNAL=""
128	_HARNESS_CLEANED_UP=0
129	
130	_test_harness_cleanup() {
131	    [[ "${_HARNESS_CLEANED_UP:-0}" == "1" ]] && return 0
132	    _HARNESS_CLEANED_UP=1
133	    _kill_test_children
134	    _test_cleanup_hook
135	    if [[ -n "${AUTO_TEST_TEMP_DIR:-}" && -d "$AUTO_TEST_TEMP_DIR" ]]; then
136	        rm -rf "$AUTO_TEST_TEMP_DIR"
137	    fi
138	    # Wave 19-L (#749): rm each named TEST_TEMP_DIR setup_test_env created
139	    # so tests that forgot _test_cleanup_hook / cleanup_test_env stop
140	    # leaking. Path-prefix guard against accidental rm-rf-/: each tracked
141	    # path must live under the source-time tmp-root captured in
142	    # _ZB_TEST_TMP_ROOT. Using the CURRENT $TMPDIR would fail when tests
143	    # re-export TMPDIR (Copilot review #751); the source-time root is
144	    # stable for the process lifetime since AUTO_TEST_TEMP_DIR was created
145	    # there. (mktemp -d always returns an absolute path so the prefix
146	    # check is meaningful.)
147	    local _trk
148	    for _trk in "${_TRACKED_TEST_TEMP_DIRS[@]:-}"; do
149	        [[ -z "$_trk" ]] && continue
150	        [[ "$_trk" == "$_ZB_TEST_TMP_ROOT"/* ]] || continue
151	        [[ -d "$_trk" ]] && rm -rf "$_trk" 2>/dev/null || true
152	    done
153	    # Signal-triggered teardown: clear both the signal trap and EXIT so the
154	    # re-raised signal exits with 128+N (143/130) without running EXIT again.
155	    if [[ -n "${_HARNESS_SIGNAL:-}" ]]; then
156	        trap - "${_HARNESS_SIGNAL}" EXIT
157	        kill -"${_HARNESS_SIGNAL}" $$
158	    fi
159	}
160	
161	# Thin wrappers installed for TERM and INT: record the in-flight signal name
162	# then call the shared cleanup body. The cleanup body re-raises at the tail
163	# so the process exits 128+signal instead of returning into the test body.
164	_harness_signal_handler() {
165	    local _sig="$1"
166	    _HARNESS_SIGNAL="$_sig"
167	    _test_harness_cleanup
168	}
169	
170	# Wave 19-L: initialize the tracking array (declared here so setup_test_env
171	# can += without `unbound variable` under set -u).
172	_TRACKED_TEST_TEMP_DIRS=()
173	trap '_test_harness_cleanup' EXIT
174	trap '_harness_signal_handler INT'  INT
175	trap '_harness_signal_handler TERM' TERM
176	
177	# ─── Assertions ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
178	
179	assert_pass() {
180	    local desc="$1"
181	    TOTAL=$((TOTAL + 1))
182	    PASS=$((PASS + 1))
183	    # #600: ZBUILD_TEST_QUIET=1 suppresses per-assertion echoes to keep the
184	    # pipeline test-stage banner compact. Counters still update; assert_fail
185	    # is intentionally NOT gated (failures always surface).
186	    [[ "${ZBUILD_TEST_QUIET:-0}" == "1" ]] && return 0
187	    echo -e "  ${GREEN}✓${RESET} ${desc}"
188	}
189	
190	assert_fail() {
191	    local desc="$1"
192	    local detail="${2:-}"
193	    TOTAL=$((TOTAL + 1))
194	    FAIL=$((FAIL + 1))
195	    FAILURES[${#FAILURES[@]}]="$desc"
196	    echo -e "  ${RED}✗${RESET} ${desc}"
197	    # An `if`, not `[[ … ]] && …` as the last line: with no detail that returned
198	    # 1, and under `set -e` the file stopped at its first failure — every later
199	    # assertion went unmeasured (#2234; 13 SPECs on #1835).
200	    if [[ -n "$detail" ]]; then echo -e "    ${DIM}${detail}${RESET}"; fi
201	    return 0
202	}
203	
204	assert_eq() {
205	    local desc="$1"
206	    local expected="$2"
207	    local actual="$3"
208	    if [[ "$expected" == "$actual" ]]; then
209	        assert_pass "$desc"
210	    else
211	        assert_fail "$desc" "expected: $expected, got: $actual"
212	    fi
213	}
214	
215	assert_contains() {
216	    local desc="$1"
217	    local haystack="$2"
218	    local needle="$3"
219	    if grep -qF -- "$needle" <<< "$haystack" 2>/dev/null; then
220	        assert_pass "$desc"
221	    else
222	        assert_fail "$desc" "output missing: $needle"
223	    fi
224	}
225	
226	assert_contains_regex() {
227	    local desc="$1"
228	    local haystack="$2"
229	    local pattern="$3"
230	    if grep -qE -- "$pattern" <<< "$haystack" 2>/dev/null; then
231	        assert_pass "$desc"
232	    else
233	        assert_fail "$desc" "output missing pattern: $pattern"
234	    fi
235	}
236	
237	assert_gt() {
238	    local desc="$1"
239	    local actual="$2"
240	    local threshold="$3"
241	    if [[ "$actual" -gt "$threshold" ]] 2>/dev/null; then
242	        assert_pass "$desc"
243	    else
244	        assert_fail "$desc" "expected >$threshold, got: $actual"
245	    fi
246	}
247	
248	assert_json_key() {
249	    local desc="$1"
250	    local json="$2"
251	    local key="$3"
252	    local expected="$4"
253	    local actual
254	    actual=$(echo "$json" | jq -r "$key" 2>/dev/null)
255	    if [[ "$actual" == "$expected" ]]; then
256	        assert_pass "$desc"
257	    else
258	        assert_fail "$desc" "key $key: expected $expected, got: $actual"
259	    fi
260	}
261	
262	assert_exit_code() {
263	    local desc="$1"
264	    local expected="$2"
265	    local actual="$3"
266	    if [[ "$expected" == "$actual" ]]; then
267	        assert_pass "$desc (exit $actual)"
268	    else
269	        assert_fail "$desc" "expected exit code: $expected, got: $actual"
270	    fi
271	}
272	
273	assert_file_exists() {
274	    local desc="$1"
275	    local filepath="$2"
276	    if [[ -f "$filepath" ]]; then
277	        assert_pass "$desc"
278	    else
279	        assert_fail "$desc" "file not found: $filepath"
280	    fi
281	}
282	
283	assert_file_not_exists() {
284	    local desc="$1"
285	    local filepath="$2"
286	    if [[ ! -f "$filepath" ]]; then
287	        assert_pass "$desc"
288	    else
289	        assert_fail "$desc" "file should not exist: $filepath"
290	    fi
291	}
292	
293	# ─── Test Environment ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
294	
295	# ─── Which engine locations a test may share (#2252 F, #1910) ────────────────
296	# Every ZBUILD_* variable naming a place the engine WRITES is cleared per test,
297	# so it falls back to the sandboxed $HOME (below) or whatever the test sets
298	# after setup. The pipeline's test stage exports ZBUILD_STATE_ROOT, a cost
299	# ledger and a cache dir for the suite it runs; clearing only STATE_DIR and
300	# ARTIFACT_DIR let every test file share one stage-io folder and seq counter
301	# (#2032 run 36969130031). tests/unit/test-env-isolation-test.sh fails on any
302	# location variable the engine reads that is in neither list.
303	_ZB_TEST_ISOLATED_VARS=(
304	    ZBUILD_STATE_ROOT ZBUILD_STATE_DIR ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR ZBUILD_STATE_FILE
305	    ZBUILD_DATA_ROOT ZBUILD_RUN_ROOT ZBUILD_POOL_ROOT ZBUILD_SCRATCH_ROOT
306	    ZBUILD_WORKTREE_ROOT ZBUILD_STAGE_INPUTS ZBUILD_STAGE_BLOCKS
307	    ZBUILD_CYCLE_FEEDBACK_DIR ZBUILD_NEGCTL_ARTIFACT_DIR
308	    ZBUILD_RUN_START_MARKER ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL
309	    ZBUILD_MEMORY_DB ZBUILD_CACHE_DIR ZBUILD_COST_LEDGER ZBUILD_ROUTER_TOOL_USES_FILE
310	    ZBUILD_WIKI_ROOT ZBUILD_INSTALL_DIR ZBUILD_BIN_DIR
311	)
312	# Code, config and the test runner's own channels: read, or deliberately shared
313	# by run-tests.sh across files (the timing file).
314	_ZB_TEST_INHERITED_VARS=(
315	    ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT ZBUILD_PLUGINS_DIR ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR ZBUILD_CORE_DIR
316	    ZBUILD_CONTRACT_LIB_DIR ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT ZBUILD_MAIN_REPO_ROOT ZBUILD_PROJECT_ROOT
317	    ZBUILD_CONFIG_FILE ZBUILD_MODELS_FILE ZBUILD_DISABLED_FILE
318	    ZBUILD_SECRET_SCAN_ALLOWLIST_FILE ZBUILD_TESTS_DIR ZBUILD_MUTATION_DIR
319	    ZBUILD_TEST_TIMING_FILE ZBUILD_TEST_DURATIONS_FILE ZBUILD_DISCOVERY_MEMO_DIR ZBUILD_RELEASE_LOCAL_DIR ZBUILD_RELEASE_VERSION_FILE
320	)
321	
322	# _zb_test_stage_blocks <dir> — the engine's three blocks for a stage that has
323	# no repository settings, no earlier stage and no manifest, written with the
324	# engine's own writers (#1799: never hand-made).
325	_zb_test_stage_blocks() {
326	    local dir="$1"
327	    (
328	        # shellcheck source=./stage-prompt.sh
329	        source "$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)/stage-prompt.sh" || exit 1
330	        mkdir -p "$dir" "$dir/repo" "$dir/state" || exit 1
331	        _stage_block_from_repo test-stage "$dir/repo" > "$dir/from-repo.md"
332	        _stage_block_previous_work test-stage "$dir/state" "$dir/plugins" "" "$dir/repo" \
333	            > "$dir/previous-work.md"
334	        _stage_block_rules test-stage "$dir/state" "$dir/no-manifest.yaml" > "$dir/rules.md"
335	    ) 2>/dev/null
336	}
337	
338	# zb_test_previous_work <state_file> <plugins_root> [consumer] — the engine's
339	# Previous work block a later stage receives (ADR-067 §8), from the engine's
340	# own writers. The flow is the caller's _TPL_STAGES.
341	zb_test_previous_work() {
342	    local state_file="$1" proot="$2" consumer="${3:-later}" sd
343	    sd="$(dirname "$state_file")"
344	    (
345	        # shellcheck source=./stage-prompt.sh
346	        source "$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)/stage-prompt.sh" || exit 1
347	        declare -F _inputs_resolve_stage >/dev/null 2>&1 \
348	            || source "$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; cd "../.." && pwd)/core/pipeline/input-resolve.sh" || exit 1
349	        _stage_block_previous_work "$consumer" "$sd" "$proot" \
350	            "$(_inputs_resolve_stage "$consumer" "$proot" "$sd")" "$sd"
351	    ) 2>/dev/null
352	}

354	setup_test_env() {
355	    local test_name="${1:-zb-test}"
356	    # Clean up auto-created temp dir and create a named one
357	    [[ -n "$TEST_TEMP_DIR" && -d "$TEST_TEMP_DIR" ]] && rm -rf "$TEST_TEMP_DIR"
358	    TEST_TEMP_DIR=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/${test_name}.XXXXXX")
359	    # Wave 19-L (#749): register the named TEST_TEMP_DIR for cleanup in the
360	    # master trap. Without this, tests that forget to set _test_cleanup_hook
361	    # or call cleanup_test_env leak the named dir. Audit (2026-06-08) found
362	    # 44 of 245 setup_test_env callsites had this gap → 1,261 leaked dirs.
363	    # The master trap (_test_harness_cleanup) reads _TRACKED_TEST_TEMP_DIRS
364	    # and rm -rf's each, in addition to AUTO_TEST_TEMP_DIR.
365	    _TRACKED_TEST_TEMP_DIRS+=("$TEST_TEMP_DIR")
366	    mkdir -p "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/home/.zbuild"
367	    mkdir -p "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin"
368	    mkdir -p "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/project"
369	    mkdir -p "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/logs"
370	
371	    # ORIG_HOME/ORIG_PATH/ORIG_STATE_DIR already saved at source time.
372	    export HOME="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/home"
373	    export PATH="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin:$PATH"
374	    # Unset ZBUILD_STATE_DIR and ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR so any ambient pipeline
375	    # values do not leak into this test process (#1713). stage-io falls back to
376	    # ${HOME}/.zbuild/state (sandboxed above) when both are unset, landing all
377	    # writes in the sandbox. We unset rather than redirect to avoid perturbing
378	    # callers that manage their own artifact paths after setup.
379	    mkdir -p "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/home/.zbuild/state"
380	    # #2252 F: every written location, not only STATE_DIR / ARTIFACT_DIR.
381	    unset "${_ZB_TEST_ISOLATED_VARS[@]}"
382	    # The event bus resolves its paths when it is SOURCED — usually before this
383	    # call, with the real $HOME — so clearing them would leave it nowhere to
384	    # write, and leaving them would write under the real ~/.zbuild. Point them
385	    # into this test's own folder; a test that wants its own sets them after.
386	    export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events"
387	    export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
388	    mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR"
389	    export NO_GITHUB=true
390	    export GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0
391	
392	    # ADR-067 §8: a stage that calls a model composes its prompt with the
393	    # engine's three blocks, which plugin_hook_call writes at dispatch. A test
394	    # that calls a stage's run function directly gets a minimal set, written by
395	    # the engine's own code; a test about the blocks sets its own.
396	    _zb_test_stage_blocks "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/stage-blocks" \
397	        && export ZBUILD_STAGE_BLOCKS="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/stage-blocks"
398	
399	    # Prevent CI-environment leakage into the test subprocess.
400	    # GitHub Actions exports WORKSPACE_BRANCH and (in some workflows) CI_MODE; if
401	    # those leak into stage-level unit tests they silently divert intake into the
402	    # CI-workspace-branch path, breaking branch-creation assertions.
403	    unset WORKSPACE_BRANCH CI_MODE
404	
405	    # Link real jq if available
406	    if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
407	        ln -sf "$(command -v jq)" "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/jq"
408	    fi
409	
410	    # Mock timeout — macOS doesn't have GNU coreutils timeout by default
411	    if ! command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then
412	        cat > "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/timeout" <<'TIMEOUT_EOF'
413	#!/usr/bin/env bash
414	shift  # skip the timeout duration
415	exec "$@"
416	TIMEOUT_EOF
417	        chmod +x "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/timeout"
418	    fi
419	
420	    # Sandbox mktemp shim — macOS only (see auto-init comment above for rationale).
421	    mkdir -p "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/_tmp"
422	    if [[ "$(uname -s 2>/dev/null)" == "Darwin" ]]; then
423	        printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\n_s="%s"\nif [[ $# -eq 0 ]]; then exec /usr/bin/mktemp "$_s/tmp.XXXXXX"; fi\nif [[ $# -eq 1 && "$1" == "-d" ]]; then exec /usr/bin/mktemp -d "$_s/tmpd.XXXXXX"; fi\nexec /usr/bin/mktemp "$@"\n' \
424	            "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/_tmp" > "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/mktemp"
425	        chmod +x "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/mktemp"
426	    fi
427	}

429	# ─── Reserved test identity (#1921 follow-up) ───────────────────────────────
430	# Tests used real issue numbers as identity fixtures — 25 of the 29 in use were
431	# live issues or PRs, and #42 is still OPEN. A run keyed to one of those writes
432	# fabricated prior work onto that issue's state branch; measured on this repo,
433	# zbuild/state/issue-999 held 68 commits of test payloads and issue-698 held 121.
434	# Now that CI chains and pushes (#1970, #2006), that reaches origin.
435	#
436	# 9_0000000+ is unreachable: this repo is ~2000 issues in. A stray
437	# zbuild/state/issue-9xxxxxxx ref is therefore unmistakably test residue, safe to
438	# reclaim, and can never be confused with someone's work.
439	# The floor of the reserved range. Read by lint-test-identity and the hygiene
440	# test; zb_test_issue composes its ids to always land at or above it.
441	ZB_TEST_ISSUE_FLOOR=90000000
442	export ZB_TEST_ISSUE_FLOOR
443	
444	# Sequential within a test file: 90000001, 90000002, … Files repeat the same ids,
445	# which is safe because each runs in its own throwaway repo — and if one ever
446	# escapes, the number identifies it instantly.
447	# The counter lives in a FILE, not a shell variable: callers use $(zb_test_issue),
448	# which runs in a subshell, so an in-memory counter would never advance and every
449	# call would return the same id.
450	#
451	# The id is keyed on the PID so two test files running in PARALLEL never mint the
452	# same one. They otherwise all start at 90000001, and the teardown below deletes
453	# refs from the SHARED checkout — so one file's cleanup could delete a ref another
454	# file was still asserting on. The unit tier is parallel by default (#984), and
455	# more cores make that likelier, which is why it showed on Linux CI first.
456	#
457	# Shape: 9 + PID%1000 (3) + seq (4) — always 8 digits, always >= 90000000.
458	zb_test_issue() {
459	    local dir="${TEST_TEMP_DIR:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}"
460	    local f="$dir/.zb-test-issue-seq"
461	    local n=0
462	    [[ -r "$f" ]] && n="$(cat "$f" 2>/dev/null || printf '0')"
463	    [[ "$n" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || n=0
464	    n=$(( n + 1 ))
465	    printf '%d' "$n" > "$f" 2>/dev/null || true
466	    local id
467	    id="$(printf '9%03d%04d' "$(( $$ % 1000 ))" "$n")"
468	    # Record it, so teardown removes exactly the refs THIS file minted rather
469	    # than every reserved ref it happens to find.
470	    printf '%s\n' "$id" >> "$dir/.zb-test-issue-minted" 2>/dev/null || true
471	    printf '%s' "$id"
472	}
473	
474	# Goal fixtures get the same treatment: the marker makes zbuild/state/goal-<hash>
475	# traceable back to a test even though the hash itself is opaque.
476	#
477	# The hash is RECORDED as it is handed out, exactly as zb_test_issue records ids.
478	# Without that, goal refs had no teardown and no guard — which is precisely how
479	# the leak fixed in this branch survived a full identity sweep unnoticed. The
480	# derivation mirrors zbuild_goal_key: sha256 of the text with all whitespace
481	# stripped, truncated to 12 hex.
482	zb_test_goal() {
483	    local text; text="$(printf '[zb-test] %s' "${1:-fixture}")"
484	    local dir="${TEST_TEMP_DIR:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}"
485	    local h
486	    h="$(printf '%s' "$text" | tr -d '[:space:]' | shasum -a 256 | cut -c1-12)"
487	    printf '%s\n' "$h" >> "$dir/.zb-test-goal-minted" 2>/dev/null || true
488	    printf '%s' "$text"
489	}

491	# A throwaway repo WITH an origin. setup_git_temp_repo builds the working tree;
492	# this adds the bare remote a push needs. Promoted out of persist-stage-test.sh,
493	# where it lived as _mk_repo.
494	zb_test_repo() {
495	    local name="${1:-zbrepo}"
496	    local remote="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/$name-remote.git"
497	    local repo
498	    repo="$(setup_git_temp_repo "$name")" || return 1
499	    local real_git; real_git="$(command -v git 2>/dev/null || echo /usr/bin/git)"
500	    (
501	        "$real_git" init -q --bare "$remote"
502	        cd "$repo" || exit 1
503	        "$real_git" remote add origin "$remote"
504	        "$real_git" push -q -u origin main
505	    ) >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
506	    printf '%s\n' "$repo"
507	}

509	# Reserved-range state refs in a repo (default: the real checkout). Used by both
510	# the teardown below and the suite-wide hygiene guard.
511	# shellcheck disable=SC2120  # callers live in tests/, which CI's shellcheck step
512	# does not scan (it covers scripts core plugins), so the optional repo argument
513	# looks unpassed from inside this file alone.
514	zb_test_reserved_refs() {
515	    local repo="${1:-${REPO_ROOT:-$PWD}}"
516	    # Prefix glob, then a NUMERIC filter — not 'issue-9???????'. That counted
517	    # characters, so it covered 90000000-99999999 only, while lint-test-identity
518	    # and _cleanup_issue_ref_decision both gate on >= 90000000. An id above the
519	    # 8-digit range would have passed both and been invisible here.
520	    local _ref _n
521	    while IFS= read -r _ref; do
522	        [[ -n "$_ref" ]] || continue
523	        _n="${_ref##*/issue-}"
524	        [[ "$_n" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue
525	        # An explicit if, not `[[ … ]] && printf`: the && form returns non-zero
526	        # when the test is false, and as the last command in the loop body that
527	        # aborts callers running under `set -e`.
528	        if [[ "$_n" -ge "${ZB_TEST_ISSUE_FLOOR:-90000000}" ]]; then
529	            printf '%s\n' "$_ref"
530	        fi
531	    done < <(git -C "$repo" for-each-ref --format='%(refname)' \
532	        'refs/heads/zbuild/state/issue-9*' 2>/dev/null || true)
533	}

535	cleanup_test_env() {
536	    # Remove state refs THIS FILE minted and may have written into the real
537	    # checkout. Deliberately not "every reserved ref present": the unit tier runs
538	    # in parallel, so deleting another file's in-flight ref would fail its
539	    # assertions. Reserved-range by construction, so a real issue's branch is
540	    # never touched — not even one already contaminated.
541	    local _minted="${TEST_TEMP_DIR:-}/.zb-test-issue-minted"
542	    if [[ -n "${TEST_TEMP_DIR:-}" && -r "$_minted" ]]; then
543	        local _id
544	        while IFS= read -r _id; do
545	            [[ "$_id" =~ ^9[0-9]{7}$ ]] || continue
546	            git -C "${REPO_ROOT:-$PWD}" update-ref -d \
547	                "refs/heads/zbuild/state/issue-$_id" 2>/dev/null || true
548	        done < "$_minted"
549	    fi
550	    local _gminted="${TEST_TEMP_DIR:-}/.zb-test-goal-minted"
551	    if [[ -n "${TEST_TEMP_DIR:-}" && -r "$_gminted" ]]; then
552	        local _h
553	        while IFS= read -r _h; do
554	            [[ "$_h" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{12}$ ]] || continue
555	            git -C "${REPO_ROOT:-$PWD}" update-ref -d \
556	                "refs/heads/zbuild/state/goal-$_h" 2>/dev/null || true
557	        done < "$_gminted"
558	    fi
559	
560	    if [[ -n "$TEST_TEMP_DIR" && -d "$TEST_TEMP_DIR" ]]; then
561	        rm -rf "$TEST_TEMP_DIR" 2>/dev/null || true
562	    fi
563	    [[ -n "${ORIG_HOME:-}" ]] && export HOME="$ORIG_HOME" || true
564	    [[ -n "${ORIG_PATH:-}" ]] && export PATH="$ORIG_PATH" || true
565	    # Restore ZBUILD_STATE_DIR and ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR to pre-setup values
566	    # (or unset them if they were not set before this test sourced the helpers).
567	    if [[ -n "${ORIG_STATE_DIR_SET:-}" ]]; then
568	        export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$ORIG_STATE_DIR"
569	    else
570	        unset ZBUILD_STATE_DIR
571	    fi
572	    if [[ -n "${ORIG_ARTIFACT_DIR_SET:-}" ]]; then
573	        export ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR="$ORIG_ARTIFACT_DIR"
574	    else
575	        unset ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR
576	    fi
577	}

621	# Install an envelope-aware mock claude binary on PATH ($TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin).
622	# Branches on argv: when invoked with `--output-format json` (ADR-018 Pattern 1
623	# decision #8, #476), wraps the payload in a {type:result,result:...} envelope
624	# so the router's `.result` extraction finds it. Otherwise emits the payload
625	# as raw text (legacy text-mode callers).
626	#
627	# Usage:
628	#   install_envelope_mock_claude <payload>                        # payload is inline text
629	#   install_envelope_mock_claude --file <payload_file>            # payload comes from a file at call time
630	#   install_envelope_mock_claude --record-argv <path> <payload>   # also record argv to <path>
631	#   install_envelope_mock_claude --record-prompt <path> <payload> # also record `-p <prompt>` to <path>
632	#
633	# Flags may be combined (e.g. --file + --record-argv).
634	install_envelope_mock_claude() {
635	    local payload="" payload_file="" argv_record="" prompt_record=""
636	    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
637	        case "$1" in
638	            --file)          payload_file="$2"; shift 2 ;;
639	            --record-argv)   argv_record="$2"; shift 2 ;;
640	            --record-prompt) prompt_record="$2"; shift 2 ;;
641	            *)               payload="$1"; shift ;;
642	        esac
643	    done
644	    mkdir -p "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin"
645	    local mock_bin="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/claude"
646	    cat > "$mock_bin" <<MOCK
647	#!/usr/bin/env bash
648	# Auto-generated by install_envelope_mock_claude (#476).
649	if [[ -n "${argv_record:-}" ]]; then
650	    printf '%s\n' "\$@" > "$argv_record"
651	fi
652	envelope_mode=0
653	prompt_text=""
654	while [[ \$# -gt 0 ]]; do
655	    case "\$1" in
656	        --output-format|json) envelope_mode=1; shift ;;
657	        -p) prompt_text="\${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
658	        *)  shift ;;
659	    esac
660	done
661	# The router sends the prompt on stdin (#1849: argv overflowed at 128 KiB).
662	[[ -n "\$prompt_text" ]] || prompt_text="\$(cat)"
663	if [[ -n "${prompt_record:-}" ]]; then
664	    printf '%s' "\$prompt_text" > "$prompt_record"
665	fi
666	if [[ -n "${payload_file:-}" ]]; then
667	    payload="\$(cat "$payload_file")"
668	else
669	    payload=$(printf '%q' "$payload")
670	fi
671	if [[ \$envelope_mode -eq 1 ]]; then
672	    jq -n --arg r "\$payload" '{type:"result",subtype:"success",result:\$r,usage:{input_tokens:0,output_tokens:0},tool_uses:[]}'
673	else
674	    printf '%s\n' "\$payload"
675	fi
676	exit 0
677	MOCK
678	    chmod +x "$mock_bin"
679	}

681	# Install an envelope-aware ERROR mock claude binary on PATH ($TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin).
682	# Mirrors install_envelope_mock_claude but simulates a failed `claude` run that
683	# still prints a JSON result envelope to stdout and exits non-zero — the exact
684	# shape route.sh persists to its diagnostic sidecar
685	# (${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-…/artifacts}/stage-io/<stage>-sync-error.raw-claude-output.json).
686	#
687	# The default envelope simulates the #1052 dogfood failure: the planner burned
688	# all its turns exploring the repo and hit max_turns before emitting plan.json:
689	#   {"type":"result","subtype":"error_max_turns","is_error":true,
690	#    "num_turns":<N>,"result":"<partial reasoning text>",
691	#    "usage":{input_tokens:…,output_tokens:…}}
692	# then `exit 1`.
693	#
694	# Everything is tunable via env vars read AT MOCK-INVOCATION TIME (not install
695	# time), so a test can export a different value just before calling plan_run and
696	# the same installed binary honors it. This lets one installer cover three cases:
697	#   (a) max_turns exhaustion (defaults).
698	#   (b) a non-max_turns crash — set ZBUILD_MOCK_SUBTYPE to e.g. "error" and the
699	#       discriminator (subtype != error_max_turns) stays on the
700	#       claude_cli_failed path.
701	#   (c) a max_turns envelope whose .result IS a valid plan.json — set
702	#       ZBUILD_MOCK_RESULT to the plan JSON; recovery should salvage it.
703	#
704	# Env vars (all optional):
705	#   ZBUILD_MOCK_SUBTYPE    envelope .subtype     (default: error_max_turns)
706	#   ZBUILD_MOCK_NUM_TURNS  envelope .num_turns   (default: 25)
707	#   ZBUILD_MOCK_RESULT     envelope .result      (default: a partial-reasoning blurb)
708	#   ZBUILD_MOCK_RC         process exit code     (default: 1)
709	#   ZBUILD_MOCK_IS_ERROR   envelope .is_error    (default: true)
710	#
711	# Usage:
712	#   install_envelope_mock_claude_error                       # max_turns defaults
713	#   install_envelope_mock_claude_error --record-argv <path>  # also record argv
714	#   install_envelope_mock_claude_error --record-prompt <path> # also record -p prompt
715	#
716	# Flags may be combined. Mirrors install_envelope_mock_claude's recording hooks
717	# so resume/dogfood tests can assert the captured prompt across runs.
718	install_envelope_mock_claude_error() {
719	    local argv_record="" prompt_record=""
720	    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
721	        case "$1" in
722	            --record-argv)   argv_record="$2"; shift 2 ;;
723	            --record-prompt) prompt_record="$2"; shift 2 ;;
724	            *)               shift ;;
725	        esac
726	    done
727	    mkdir -p "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin"
728	    local mock_bin="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/claude"
729	    cat > "$mock_bin" <<MOCK
730	#!/usr/bin/env bash
731	# Auto-generated by install_envelope_mock_claude_error (#1052).
732	if [[ -n "${argv_record:-}" ]]; then
733	    printf '%s\n' "\$@" > "$argv_record"
734	fi
735	prompt_text=""
736	while [[ \$# -gt 0 ]]; do
737	    case "\$1" in
738	        -p) prompt_text="\${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
739	        *)  shift ;;
740	    esac
741	done
742	# The router sends the prompt on stdin (#1849: argv overflowed at 128 KiB).
743	[[ -n "\$prompt_text" ]] || prompt_text="\$(cat)"
744	if [[ -n "${prompt_record:-}" ]]; then
745	    printf '%s' "\$prompt_text" > "$prompt_record"
746	fi
747	# Tunable envelope fields — read at invocation time so a test can vary the
748	# shape per call without reinstalling the mock.
749	_subtype="\${ZBUILD_MOCK_SUBTYPE:-error_max_turns}"
750	_num_turns="\${ZBUILD_MOCK_NUM_TURNS:-25}"
751	_is_error="\${ZBUILD_MOCK_IS_ERROR:-true}"
752	_rc="\${ZBUILD_MOCK_RC:-1}"
753	_result="\${ZBUILD_MOCK_RESULT:-Explored core/ and plugins/ but ran out of turns before emitting a complete plan. Partial findings: the change touches the router and the plan plugin.}"
754	jq -n \\
755	    --arg st "\$_subtype" \\
756	    --argjson nt "\$_num_turns" \\
757	    --argjson ie "\$_is_error" \\
758	    --arg r "\$_result" \\
759	    '{type:"result",subtype:\$st,is_error:\$ie,num_turns:\$nt,result:\$r,usage:{input_tokens:0,output_tokens:0},tool_uses:[]}'
760	exit "\$_rc"
761	MOCK
762	    chmod +x "$mock_bin"
763	}

765	# ─── Platform Skip Guards ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
766	
767	# Fail loudly on an unknown platform argument. A typo (e.g. `lniux`) must NOT
768	# silently skip a test forever while still reporting success — that would let CI
769	# mask a test that never runs. Exits non-zero so the mistake surfaces.
770	_require_known_platform() {
771	    case "$1" in
772	        linux|macos) return 0 ;;
773	        *)
774	            echo -e "  ${RED}ERROR${RESET}: unknown platform '$1' (expected: linux|macos)" >&2
775	            exit 2
776	            ;;
777	    esac
778	}

780	skip_unless_platform() {
781	    local required="$1"
782	    _require_known_platform "$required"
783	    local current
784	    current="$(uname -s 2>/dev/null)"
785	    case "$current" in
786	        Darwin) current="macos" ;;
787	        Linux)  current="linux" ;;
788	    esac
789	    [[ "$current" == "$required" ]] && return 0
790	    SKIP=$((SKIP + 1))
791	    echo -e "  ${YELLOW}SKIP${RESET}: requires '$required', running on '$current'" >&2
792	    print_test_results
793	}
794	
795	skip_on_platform() {
796	    local excluded="$1"
797	    _require_known_platform "$excluded"
798	    local current
799	    current="$(uname -s 2>/dev/null)"
800	    case "$current" in
801	        Darwin) current="macos" ;;
802	        Linux)  current="linux" ;;
803	    esac
804	    [[ "$current" != "$excluded" ]] && return 0
805	    SKIP=$((SKIP + 1))
806	    echo -e "  ${YELLOW}SKIP${RESET}: excluded on '$excluded'" >&2
807	    print_test_results
808	}

810	# Capability gate: SKIP cleanly when the platform is right but a required tool is
811	# absent or lacks a needed feature, so an unexercisable contract is an honest
812	# SKIP instead of a confusing failure. Args: a human-readable label, then a probe
813	# command (+args) run with output suppressed — e.g.
814	#   skip_unless_capable "setsid -w unavailable" setsid -w true
815	#   skip_unless_capable "flock unavailable" command -v flock
816	skip_unless_capable() {
817	    local label="$1"; shift
818	    "$@" >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0
819	    SKIP=$((SKIP + 1))
820	    echo -e "  ${YELLOW}SKIP${RESET}: $label" >&2
821	    print_test_results

1053	# ─── zb_test_kill_tree <pid> ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
1054	# KILL <pid> and every process under it. KILL cannot be caught, so a runner
1055	# killed alone cleans up nothing: its forked stage and the stage's time-limit
1056	# watchdog (copies of its shell, so they show as runner.sh) ran on, the watchdog
1057	# for up to the stage's limit.
1058	#
1059	# Deepest first, so no parent dies before its children (a child whose parent is
1060	# gone is re-parented away and can no longer be found), and read again until
1061	# nothing is left, for a child forked while the tree was being read. Nothing is
1062	# STOPped on the way: a stopped process whose parent dies leaves an orphaned
1063	# process group with a stopped member, and the kernel hangs up that whole group
1064	# — on macOS CI, the test's own. A process already gone is no error, under
1065	# set -e too: an abort test's runner has usually exited on its TERM by then.
1066	_zb_test_tree() { local c; printf '%s\n' "$1"; for c in $(pgrep -P "$1" 2>/dev/null || true); do _zb_test_tree "$c"; done; }
1067	zb_test_kill_tree() {
1068	    local -a t
1069	    local i r
1070	    for (( r = 0; r < 5; r++ )); do
1071	        mapfile -t t < <(_zb_test_tree "$1")
1072	        for (( i = ${#t[@]} - 1; i >= 0; i-- )); do kill -KILL "${t[i]}" 2>/dev/null || true; done
1073	        kill -0 "$1" 2>/dev/null || (( ${#t[@]} > 1 )) || break
1074	    done
1075	    return 0
1076	}

1078	# Bounded poll for a grep pattern to appear in an events/state file (#619's
1079	# "wait-for-event-content" pattern; reused by #887/#1127/#1149). Replaces the
1080	# anti-pattern of a fixed `sleep N` followed by a single-shot read of an
1081	# event/state file — that races a slow CI box (the writer may not have flushed
1082	# the line yet). This polls the file until the content appears, bounded by a
1083	# generous timeout so a genuinely-never-emitted event still fails fast-enough
1084	# instead of hanging.
1085	#
1086	# Usage: wait_for_event <file> <grep_pattern> [max_iters=600] [interval=0.1]
1087	#   - <grep_pattern> is a basic-regex passed to `grep -q` (quote JSON fragments,
1088	#     e.g. '"pipeline.start"').
1089	#   - Default bound: 600 × 0.1s = 60s — generous enough for a loaded shared CI
1090	#     runner, short enough to never wedge the suite.
1091	# Returns 0 as soon as the pattern is present; 1 if the bound elapses first.
1092	# Does NOT assert — callers decide whether a timeout is fatal so the failure
1093	# message stays test-specific.
1094	wait_for_event() {
1095	    local file="$1" pattern="$2" max_iters="${3:-600}" interval="${4:-0.1}" i
1096	    for (( i = 0; i < max_iters; i++ )); do
1097	        if [[ -f "$file" ]] && grep -q "$pattern" "$file" 2>/dev/null; then
1098	            return 0
1099	        fi
1100	        sleep "$interval"
1101	    done
1102	    return 1
1103	}

1128	# ─── setup_git_temp_repo ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1129	# Creates a real, minimal git repo under $TEST_TEMP_DIR/<name> with one
1130	# initial commit. Returns its absolute path on stdout. Used by integration
1131	# tests that exercise real `git checkout`/`git symbolic-ref` against an
1132	# isolated repo (issue #484).
1133	#
1134	# Usage:
1135	#   repo="$(setup_git_temp_repo myrepo)"
1136	#   (cd "$repo" && some_test)

1138	    local name="${1:-gitrepo}"
1139	    local repo="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/$name"
1140	    mkdir -p "$repo" 2>/dev/null || return 1
1141	    (
1142	        # #2103 / ADR-024: the cd MUST be fatal. `set -e` is inert inside this
1143	        # subshell because its status is tested by `|| return 1` below, so a
1144	        # failed cd would otherwise run every git command in the CALLER'S
1145	        # checkout — which is exactly what committed seed.txt into a real
1146	        # worktree and pushed a branch to the real origin on 2026-09-15.
1147	        cd "$repo" || exit 1
1148	        # Use the real git binary (not whatever PATH shim may be present).
1149	        local real_git
1150	        real_git="$(command -v git 2>/dev/null || true)"
1151	        # If a shim like the parity-fixture mock is on PATH, fall back to
1152	        # well-known absolute locations.
1153	        if [[ -z "$real_git" ]]; then
1154	            for c in /usr/bin/git /usr/local/bin/git /opt/homebrew/bin/git; do
1155	                [[ -x "$c" ]] && real_git="$c" && break
1156	            done
1157	        fi
1158	        [[ -z "$real_git" ]] && return 1
1159	        "$real_git" init -q -b main 2>/dev/null || "$real_git" init -q
1160	        "$real_git" config user.email "test@zbuild.local"
1161	        "$real_git" config user.name "zbuild-test"
1162	        "$real_git" config commit.gpgsign false
1163	        echo "seed" > seed.txt
1164	        "$real_git" add seed.txt
1165	        "$real_git" commit -q -m "seed"
1166	        # Normalize default branch name to 'main' for predictable tests.
1167	        local cur
1168	        cur="$("$real_git" symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo main)"
1169	        if [[ "$cur" != "main" ]]; then
1170	            "$real_git" branch -m "$cur" main 2>/dev/null || true
1171	        fi
1172	    ) >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
1173	    printf '%s\n' "$repo"

1176	# ── setup_git_master_origin (#2103) ──────────────────────────────────────────
1177	# A bare origin whose default branch is `master` (not `main`), seeded with one
1178	# commit, plus a working clone of it whose origin/HEAD → origin/master. Prints
1179	# the clone's path; prints nothing and returns 1 on any setup failure. Extracted
1180	# from tests/integration/intake-branch-ahead-count-test.sh, where a failed seed
1181	# clone let the seeding subshell run — and `git push origin HEAD:master` — in
1182	# the caller's checkout against the caller's origin. Every cd here is fatal
1183	# because each subshell's status is tested (see setup_git_temp_repo).
1184	#
1185	# Usage:
1186	#   clone="$(setup_git_master_origin a)" || fail "setup"
1187	setup_git_master_origin() {
1188	    local label="${1:-m}"
1189	    local bare="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bare-${label}.git"
1190	    local work="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/work-${label}"
1191	    local tmp_init="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/init-${label}"
1192	
1193	    git init --bare "$bare" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { printf ''; return 1; }
1194	    git -C "$bare" symbolic-ref HEAD "refs/heads/master" 2>/dev/null || { printf ''; return 1; }
1195	
1196	    # Seed via a throwaway clone. The clone's OWN rc is checked before the
1197	    # subshell so a clone failure never reaches the cd; the cd is fatal anyway.
1198	    git clone "$bare" "$tmp_init" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { printf ''; return 1; }
1199	    (
1200	        cd "$tmp_init" || exit 1
1201	        git config user.email "test@zbuild.local" || exit 1
1202	        git config user.name "zbuild-test" || exit 1
1203	        git config commit.gpgsign false || exit 1
1204	        # Unborn HEAD: -b names the branch regardless of init.defaultBranch.
1205	        git checkout -q -b master 2>/dev/null || git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/master || exit 1
1206	        echo "seed" > seed.txt || exit 1
1207	        git add seed.txt || exit 1
1208	        git commit -q -m "seed" || exit 1
1209	        git push -q origin HEAD:"refs/heads/master" || exit 1
1210	    ) >/dev/null 2>&1 || { printf ''; return 1; }
1211	    rm -rf "$tmp_init"
1212	
1213	    # The bare repo MUST now carry master; a bare `.git` check downstream cannot
1214	    # tell "seeded" from "empty", and an unborn HEAD makes `checkout master` a no-op.
1215	    git -C "$bare" show-ref --verify --quiet refs/heads/master || { printf ''; return 1; }
1216	
1217	    git clone "$bare" "$work" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { printf ''; return 1; }
1218	    (
1219	        cd "$work" || exit 1
1220	        git config user.email "test@zbuild.local" || exit 1
1221	        git config user.name "zbuild-test" || exit 1
1222	        git config commit.gpgsign false || exit 1
1223	    ) >/dev/null 2>&1 || { printf ''; return 1; }
1224	
1225	    printf '%s\n' "$work"

1228	# ── install_template_overlay (#1270) ─────────────────────────────────────────
1229	# Copy one or more template fixtures into a repo's per-repo override dir
1230	# (<repo>/.zbuild/templates/<id>.yaml), the generic ADR-016 overlay seam. A test
1231	# that then runs the engine with CWD = <repo> resolves the fixture WITHOUT any
1232	# env var and WITHOUT writing into the tracked config/templates/ — the overlay
1233	# lives entirely inside the test's temp repo (reaped by the master EXIT/INT/TERM
1234	# trap). This replaces the #1268 ZBUILD_TEMPLATES_DIR seam (reverted in #1270):
1235	# no ambient env, no global state; hermeticity comes from CWD isolation.
1236	#
1237	# Each fixture is a `.zbuild/templates/` overlay, so it MUST carry `extends: <id>`
1238	# (ADR-016). The shipped base it extends (usually `simple`) is read from the
1239	# engine tree unchanged — only the overlay id needs a fixture.
1240	#
1241	# Usage: install_template_overlay <repo> <id> [<id> ...]
1242	# install_simple_loop_continue <repo> — overlay template `simple-loop-continue`:
1243	# the shipped simple.yaml with delivery_loop set to on_max: continue.
1244	# #2241: simple.yaml's outer loop is on_max: halt, and the runner honours it.
1245	# Tests whose subject is the CONTINUE path past an exhausted loop (#766, #1217)
1246	# drive this instead — generated from the real template at test time, so it
1247	# never drifts from it. (#2369: the design loop it once also changed is retired.)
1248	install_simple_loop_continue() {
1249	    local _repo="${1:?install_simple_loop_continue: <repo> required}" _src_root
1250	    _src_root="$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; cd "../.." && pwd)"
1251	    mkdir -p "$_repo/.zbuild/templates"
1252	    awk '
1253	        /^id: simple$/ { print "id: simple-loop-continue"; print "extends: simple"; next }
1254	        /^delivery_loop:/ { in_dl = 1; print; next }
1255	        in_dl && /^[a-z_-]+:/ { in_dl = 0 }
1256	        in_dl && /^  on_max: halt$/ { print "  on_max: continue"; next }
1257	        { print }
1258	    ' "$_src_root/config/templates/simple.yaml" > "$_repo/.zbuild/templates/simple-loop-continue.yaml"
1259	    grep -q '^id: simple-loop-continue$' "$_repo/.zbuild/templates/simple-loop-continue.yaml" || return 1
1260	    # Committed, as install_template_overlay_committed does: an untracked
1261	    # overlay leaves the tree dirty and intake refuses to start on it.
1262	    local _git; _git="$(command -v git 2>/dev/null || echo /usr/bin/git)"
1263	    "$_git" -C "$_repo" add .zbuild/templates >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
1264	    "$_git" -C "$_repo" commit -q -m "add test template overlay" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
1265	}
1266	
1267	install_template_overlay() {
1268	    local _repo="$1"; shift
1269	    # Fail fast on an empty repo arg (e.g. an unset OVERLAY_REPO): otherwise we'd
1270	    # mkdir/cp into /.zbuild/templates and fail later with a confusing error.
1271	    if [[ -z "$_repo" ]]; then
1272	        echo "install_template_overlay: <repo> argument required (got empty)" >&2
1273	        return 1
1274	    fi
1275	    mkdir -p "$_repo/.zbuild/templates"
1276	    # The overlay is test setup, not work: kept out of `git status` so the
1277	    # engine's dirty-tree check (#2367) does not refuse the run.
1278	    if [[ -d "$_repo/.git/info" ]] && ! grep -qxF '/.zbuild/' "$_repo/.git/info/exclude" 2>/dev/null; then
1279	        printf '/.zbuild/\n' >> "$_repo/.git/info/exclude"
1280	    fi
1281	    # Repo root derived from THIS helper's location (…/scripts/lib → repo root),
1282	    # not the caller's cwd, so it resolves regardless of where the test runs.
1283	    local _hdir _src_root
1284	    _hdir="$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)"
1285	    _src_root="$(cd "$_hdir/../.." && pwd)"
1286	    local _id _src
1287	    for _id in "$@"; do
1288	        _src="$_src_root/tests/fixtures/templates/${_id}.yaml"
1289	        if [[ ! -f "$_src" ]]; then
1290	            echo "install_template_overlay: fixture not found: $_src" >&2
1291	            return 1
1292	        fi
1293	        cp "$_src" "$_repo/.zbuild/templates/${_id}.yaml"
1294	    done
1295	}
1296	
1297	# install_template_overlay_committed <repo> <id> [<id> ...]
1298	# Like install_template_overlay, but COMMITS the overlay into the repo's git
1299	# HEAD. Needed when the runner (or a nested runner) rsyncs the repo and runs
1300	# `git checkout HEAD -- . && git clean -fdq`, which would wipe an untracked
1301	# overlay (state-root-isolation section F, SPEC-7).
1302	install_template_overlay_committed() {
1303	    local _repo="$1"
1304	    install_template_overlay "$@" || return 1
1305	    local real_git
1306	    real_git="$(command -v git 2>/dev/null || true)"
1307	    if [[ -z "$real_git" ]]; then
1308	        for c in /usr/bin/git /usr/local/bin/git /opt/homebrew/bin/git; do
1309	            [[ -x "$c" ]] && real_git="$c" && break
1310	        done
1311	    fi
1312	    [[ -z "$real_git" ]] && { echo "install_template_overlay_committed: git not found" >&2; return 1; }
1313	    "$real_git" -C "$_repo" add .zbuild/templates >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
1314	    "$real_git" -C "$_repo" commit -q -m "add test template overlay" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
1315	}
